name: legacy-v6-refit
description: The v6 transformer final refit rebuild_all.py hard-coded as SHIPPING_RECIPES['v6'] until 2026-10-09, verbatim, plus the --epochs 80 it passed by default. rebuild_all.py --v6 trains this.
notes: Not measured: no seed panel ran on this flag set, and its reported metrics are in-sample. --phase final-refit fits every row, val and test included, while the report labels its held-out recall, CQS and promote verdict 'selection_holdout' [training#0]. With --val-every 10 and --checkpoint-metric cqs the restored epoch is also chosen by val recall on rows the model trained on.

--epochs 80 is not in SHIPPING_RECIPES: it was rebuild_all.py's EPOCHS_DEFAULT and train.sh's EPOCHS_REFIT. It is here because rebuild_all.py now passes --epochs only when asked (--epochs, --quick 40, --full 150), so --recipe legacy-v6-refit still trains what the old default --v6 run trained.

Against what train.sh --v6 passed before it became a wrapper over rebuild_all.py (645e153b): train.sh also passed --val-every 5, which this recipe leaves at the default 10 (validation and checkpoint candidates every 10 epochs instead of 5, so a different restored epoch and a different training run), and --hard-neg-boost 0.4, which is the default (no difference). Both passed --batch 512 --seed 7 and no --device, so both trained on cpu. The wrapper dropped --val-every 5 without saying so; a reviewer found it.

Against the measure recipe: transformer fusion with 40-wide, 192-hidden, 3-block towers, d_model 128, fusion hidden 512, --drop-p 0.15, --weight-decay 0.0002, --phase final-refit against select, --era-align procrustes, --robust-scaling, and validation every 10 epochs with the cqs checkpoint against none [orchestration#3, training#6].
